source_name: WOOD & Company – Equity Research (CEE)
source_subtype: regional broker research + investor conference organiser
why_relevant: Leading CEE investment bank (Prague, founded 1991) with ~22 analysts covering ~200 companies in 15+ countries and a large Hungarian equity market share; named on OTP's own covering-analyst list. WOOD also runs the region's biggest investor conferences (Prague/Winter/Emerging Europe), whose agendas list which Hungarian bank managements meet investors.

source_name: Portfolio.hu Rendezvények / Konferencia (Hitelezés, Financial IT, Future of Finance)
why_relevant: Portfolio runs the dominant Hungarian banking/payments conference circuit — Hitelezés (~400 attendees, Banking Association president speaking), Financial IT (28 May 2026, Marriott; AI in banking), Future of Finance. Agendas, speaker lists and post-event write-ups are public and dated in both HU and EN, naming exactly which bank/payments executives are talking about what.

source_name: Seeking Alpha – OTP Bank Nyrt. (OTPBF/OTPGF) earnings call transcripts and call presentations
why_relevant: Carries full OTP earnings-call transcripts including the analyst Q&A (e.g. Q4 2025 call, 6 Mar 2026, with CEO and CFO László Bencsik) plus the Q2 2026 earnings-call presentation. The Q&A is where management says things absent from the written flash report — the core value proposition of this cell.

source_name: Investing.com / Yahoo Finance / MarketScreener – OTP earnings-call transcript mirrors
why_relevant: Multiple independent mirrors of the same OTP calls across ticker lines (OTP.BD, OTP.F, OTPT.XD, OTPGF), giving redundancy when one host is blocked and covering quarters others miss. Useful mainly as a fallback and for date/attendance metadata.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. (Hungary) – investor presentation series
source_subtype: non-listed bank investor presentation deck series
why_relevant: An unlisted Hungarian bank subsidiary nonetheless publishing dated, versioned investor presentations (Nov 2025, Feb 2026) at a stable /documents/d/bank/ path — evidence that investor-channel disclosure in HU banking extends beyond BÉT-listed issuers, driven by bond/funding investors.

source_name: BSE English mirror – Investor relations & Issuers sections (bse.hu)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the exchange's own IR and issuer pages, including company profile pages per security. Gives EN-language entry points and stable company-profile URL patterns (/pages/company_profile/$security/TICKER) for enumerating listed banks and their disclosure streams.

source_name: Budapest Stock Exchange LinkedIn page
why_relevant: BÉT announces investor days, issuer events and international roadshow appearances (e.g. Master Investor Show London, with listed companies attending, and named staff speaking on ESG and exit strategies) on LinkedIn earlier and more completely than on the corporate site; useful for catching events that never get a bet.hu event page.

source_name: EBA EU-wide Transparency Exercise (bank-by-bank CSV database)
why_relevant: Annual, harmonised, bank-by-bank supervisory disclosure (capital, RWA, P&L, exposures, NPL, sovereign exposures) covering the Hungarian banks in the EU sample (historically OTP Bank Nyrt.; MBH/Erste HU appear via parent or national samples). Full CSV database plus data dictionary makes it the single best normalised, English-language, machine-readable cross-border mirror of Hungarian bank disclosures, and it survives independently of any bank's own IR site.

source_name: EBA Credit Institutions Register
why_relevant: EU-level normalised list of authorised credit institutions including all Hungarian ones, with LEI, authorisation/withdrawal dates and national competent authority links. Authorisation-withdrawal records are the cleanest machine-readable evidence of Hungarian bank mergers (MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarek into MBH) that trigger IR-estate disappearance, so it anchors the entity timeline behind archived-site work.

source_name: EBA Central Register of Payment and E-Money Institutions (PSD2)
why_relevant: Aggregates the MNB's national PSP register into an EU-wide, daily-updated, fully downloadable dataset covering Hungarian payment institutions, EMIs, account information/payment initiation service providers and their agents and passporting. This is the single most practical cross-border route to the Hungarian PSP population in English without reading Hungarian register pages.

source_name: Ceginformacios portal / Ceginformacios Szolgalat (Ministry of Justice company register front-end)
why_relevant: Official company-register search giving registration numbers, legal successors and merger records for Hungarian banks and PSPs. Supplies the entity keys (cegjegyzekszam, tax number) that unlock e-beszamolo and the commercial aggregators, and evidences successor relationships after bank mergers.

source_name: OPTEN Cegtar / Merlegtar
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian commercial aggregator; Merlegtar normalises statutory filings from 1998 onward into Excel-ready balance sheet and P&L series, with company comparison and benchmarking reports. Free public company cards exist for the majors (OTP Bank Nyrt., MKB Bank Nyrt.), so it doubles as a low-cost lookup and as a persistent record for merged/dissolved entities.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Hungary (formerly Bisnode D&B Magyarorszag) company database
why_relevant: Cross-border aggregator that normalises Hungarian court-register and filing data into the global D&B/DUNS structure, giving English-language, comparable records for Hungarian banks, PSPs and their group parents plus ownership trees and failure-risk scores. The legacy Bisnode free search remains a cheap lookup route.

source_name: Ceginfo.hu
why_relevant: Hungarian company-data aggregator with per-entity profile pages that persist after corporate rebrands (e.g. it still carries the Bisnode D&B Magyarorszag identity for the renamed D&B Hungary entity). Useful as a redundancy layer and for legacy-name resolution when a Hungarian bank entity has been merged away.

source_name: Ceginformacio.hu (bilingual HU/EN credit report and document download service)
why_relevant: Sells authenticated Hungarian company documents and multi-year balance sheet / P&L exports in Excel, with English-language report pages - one of the few routes that hands a non-Hungarian-speaking analyst a normalised English filing extract for a Hungarian bank or PSP subsidiary.

source_name: Other Hungarian company-document resellers (onlineceginformacio.hu, cegjegyzek.hu, cegkivonat.com, cegtalalo.hu)
why_relevant: A cluster of resellers drawing on the same e-cegjegyzek / Ceginformacios Szolgalat backend, offering instant HU/EN/DE/FR certified extracts and multi-year Excel financials. Worth tracking as fallback access routes when the official portal is slow or a specific historical filing is hard to locate, and as a signal of what document types are commercially demanded.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine (retired Hungarian bank IR estates)
why_relevant: Core of this cell's rationale: mkb.hu, budapestbank.hu and takarekbank.hu IR sections were folded into mbhbank.hu, so Wayback snapshots are frequently the only surviving access route to pre-merger annual reports, quarterly releases and IR press-release indexes. Wayback also carries the full-text .hu crawl since 1996 that the national library relies on.

source_name: MNMKK OSZK Webarchivum (Hungarian national library web archive)
why_relevant: National-library archive with six-monthly snapshots of the Hungarian web space since 2017 plus thematic sub-collections - a second, jurisdictionally Hungarian archive of bank and PSP sites that can hold captures Wayback missed. Critical caveat: most of the collection is closed for copyright/privacy reasons and served only through a restricted research interface.

source_name: MBH Bank investor relations - legacy MKB/Takarek report archive
why_relevant: The successor entity has partially re-hosted the pre-merger MKB Bank Nyrt. financial reports and maintains a Takarekbank archive section - i.e. a live mirror of part of the wiped IR estate. Because re-hosted archives are themselves volatile, it should be harvested now and cross-checked against Wayback.

source_name: Budapest Stock Exchange (BET) issuer news and company data pages
why_relevant: Exchange-side mirror of issuer disclosures for OTP and other listed financials, with per-issuer company cards offering the latest annual report and downloadable data. A second copy of the MNB OAM filings, organised by ticker and usable when the OAM search is awkward; BET pages also carry HU/EN parallel content.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal / BRIS - Find a company
why_relevant: EU-level federated search across national business registers including Hungary's, exposing EUID-keyed records, branch and cross-border merger information in English. It is the canonical cross-border entry point that translates Hungarian register data for non-Hungarian users and documents exactly which HU company forms are in scope.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision - List of Supervised Entities (and RIAD master data)
why_relevant: Periodic PDF/spreadsheet lists of significant and less-significant institutions, archived monthly back years. Hungary is a non-euro, non-SSM member state so HU banks appear mainly as subsidiaries/branches of SSM groups (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, KBC/K&H) - which is exactly how a large share of the Hungarian banking market is disclosed at group level in English. RIAD underlies the entity identifiers, with MNB as the national hub.

source_name: Orbis Bank Focus (Moody's / Bureau van Dijk)
why_relevant: Global bank-financials database (c.30,000 banks, up to 30 years of accounts) that standardises Hungarian bank statements into comparable international/global-detailed formats in English, and retains records for institutions that no longer exist. The classic academic/industry route to long HU bank time series without re-parsing Hungarian PDFs.

source_name: EMIS (ISI Emerging Markets Group) Hungary company profiles
why_relevant: Emerging-markets aggregator carrying English-language Hungarian company profiles with financials and key executives, sourced from local filings and news. Particularly geared to CEE/Hungary, so it closes the language gap for HU banks, PSPs and fintechs and bundles local trade-press coverage alongside filings.

source_name: Partnerradar.hu
why_relevant: Smaller Hungarian company-intelligence aggregator with per-entity pages; useful as a third redundancy layer for entity resolution and for spotting which HU financial-sector entities are actively monitored commercially. Lower authority than Opten or D&B.

source_name: KBC Group Investor Relations — Results & Reports hub
why_relevant: Master entry point for KBC's quarterly results package (press release, quarterly report, analyst presentation, databook). K&H Bank Hungary is reported inside the International Markets business unit with its own country result line, loan/deposit volumes and commentary — the richest recurring source on K&H, published in English on a fixed quarterly calendar.

source_name: KBC Group Quarterly Report (PDF series, wcmassets CDN)
why_relevant: The actual quarterly document containing Hungary segment figures: K&H net result, NII, loan and deposit volumes, cost/income, impairments, plus Hungarian regulatory shocks (extra-profit/windfall bank and insurance tax, mortgage interest-rate cap, modification losses). Directly quotable numeric series per quarter.

source_name: KBC results distributed via GlobeNewswire / Ritzau newswire mirrors
why_relevant: Regulated-information newswires mirror the identical KBC quarterly report PDFs at publication minute. Useful as a redundancy/liveness channel when kbc.com assets rotate their CDN cache tokens, and gives a timestamped record of when the Hungary numbers became public.
